raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

#45154 adds a built-in Python chat template for GLM-5.3 and GLM-5.3-Flash: prompts are identical token for token to the checkpoints' `chat_template.jinja`, rendering is 4.7-17x faster, and request preprocessing of long agent conversations is up to 2.3x faster. This PR makes the cookbook recipes select it explicitly, so every generated launch command uses it.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Depends on #45154. This stays a draft until a release that includes it is published as `lmsysorg/sglang:latest`, because older builds reject `--chat-template glm-5.3` / `glm-5.3-flash` at startup.

## Modifications

- `docs/src/snippets/configs/zai-org/glm-5.3.jsx`: add `--chat-template glm-5.3` to the 27 NVIDIA cells (H200, B200, GB300, B300). The 15 AMD cells (MI355X, MI325X, MI300X) are unchanged because they pin `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.20-*`, which predates the flag; add it there when that image is bumped.
- `docs/src/snippets/configs/zai-org/glm-5.3-flash.jsx`: add `--chat-template glm-5.3-flash` to all 32 cells (the MI355X cells install SGLang from pip, so they get the flag with the same release as `:latest`).
- `GLM-5.3-Flash.mdx`: add the flag to the prose launch examples that serve chat requests (the encoder-disaggregation language server, prefill CP, and the PD prefill and decode servers). The encoder-only server does not render chat prompts, so it is unchanged.
- Both pages: a configuration tip on what the flag does, how `--reasoning-parser auto` / `--tool-call-parser auto` resolve with it, and how to serve a customized template instead (`--chat-template /path/to/chat_template.jinja`). The tip also scopes the flag to SGLang's default Python HTTP frontend: the Rust frontend (`SGLANG_RUST_SERVER=1`) renders GLM-5.3 from the checkpoint's template on its own and reads `--chat-template` as a file path, so its users leave the flag out.

The flag sits right before `--host`, so Playground additions such as the parsers, which are inserted before `--host`, follow it.

## Accuracy Tests

No model-output change: the flag selects a renderer whose prompt token ids equal the Jinja template's (differential fuzzing, serving-level, and online A/B results are in #45154).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

See #45154.

@@ -136,6 +136,10 @@ All strategies enable multimodal serving. Image and video input use `Glm5NextPro
 
 The default multimodal feature transport is automatic, and on a single CUDA node auto resolves to CPU transport. The MI355X selection explicitly emits CPU transport, matching its image-serving check. CUDA IPC is opt-in: pass `--mm-feature-transport cuda_ipc` when lower transfer latency matters more than the GPU memory the IPC pool reserves. CUDA VMM transport applies only to multi-node GB200/GB300 systems on the MNNVL fabric, where auto selects it.
 
+### Render prompts with the Python chat template
+
+The recipes pass `--chat-template glm-5.3-flash`, which renders prompts, including image and video placeholders, with SGLang's built-in Python port of the checkpoint's `chat_template.jinja`; it requires a build that includes [PR #45154](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/45154). Prompts are identical token for token, rendering is 4.7–17x faster, and request preprocessing of long agent conversations is up to 1.9x faster. `--reasoning-parser auto` and `--tool-call-parser auto` still resolve to `glm45` and `glm47`. The flag applies to SGLang's default Python HTTP frontend; leave it out with the Rust frontend (`SGLANG_RUST_SERVER=1`), which renders GLM-5.3-Flash from the checkpoint's template on its own and reads `--chat-template` as a file path. To serve a customized template, pass its path instead (`--chat-template /path/to/chat_template.jinja`).
+
 ## 3. Advanced usage
 
 ### 3.1 Reasoning

@@ -109,6 +109,7 @@ import { Playground } from "/src/snippets/_playground.jsx";
 - **BF16 weights need more GPUs.** The full-precision build (`zai-org/GLM-5.3-BF16`, ~1.5 TB) does not fit a single 8×H200 / 8×B200 / 4×GB300 node. It fits single-node on **8×B300** (TP8, ~2.1 TB HBM); on the smaller GPUs it needs a **multi-node** layout (e.g. 2×8×H200 or 2×8×B200 at TP16, 2×4×GB300 at TP8). FP8 is the recommended deployment. Use the same DSA / MTP / chunked-prefill guidance as FP8.
 - **PD Disaggregation (prefill/decode).** GLM-5.3 is a DSA model and runs under prefill/decode disaggregation — toggle the **PD Disagg** card in the [Playground above](#playground) (pick a Prefill/Decode role + transfer backend, then front the roles with `sglang_router.launch_router --pd-disaggregation`). The Mooncake backend **auto-detects the InfiniBand HCA**, so no device flag is needed by default; only add `--disaggregation-ib-device mlx5_0` (your NIC) if auto-detection picks the wrong device or KV transfer fails to connect. On H200 Docker, expose the IB HCAs to the container (`--privileged --ulimit memlock=-1`, or `--device /dev/infiniband:/dev/infiniband --cap-add IPC_LOCK`) — without IB exposure Mooncake silently falls back to TCP.
 - **Chunked-prefill size is regime-dependent.** For long-input balanced workloads, start with `--chunked-prefill-size 32768` and tune it together with `--max-running-requests` for your input length and KV capacity. Keep the default chunked-prefill size for the high-throughput recipe unless profiling shows that prefill is the bottleneck.
+- **Python chat template.** The NVIDIA recipes pass `--chat-template glm-5.3`, which renders prompts with SGLang's built-in Python port of the checkpoint's `chat_template.jinja`; it requires a build that includes [PR #45154](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/45154). Prompts are identical token for token, rendering is 4.7–17x faster, and request preprocessing of long agent conversations is up to 2.3x faster. `--reasoning-parser auto` and `--tool-call-parser auto` still resolve to `glm45` and `glm47`. The flag applies to SGLang's default Python HTTP frontend; leave it out with the Rust frontend (`SGLANG_RUST_SERVER=1`), which renders GLM-5.3 from the checkpoint's template on its own and reads `--chat-template` as a file path. To serve a customized template, pass its path instead (`--chat-template /path/to/chat_template.jinja`). The AMD recipes omit the flag because their pinned ROCm image predates it.
 
 - **AMD GPUs (MI300X / MI325X / MI355X).** FP8 (`zai-org/GLM-5.3`) runs single-node at `tp=8` on all three. BF16 (`zai-org/GLM-5.3-BF16`, ~1.51 TB) only fits single-node on **MI325X** (2 TB HBM) and **MI355X** (2.3 TB); **MI300X** (1.5 TB) cannot hold the BF16 weights plus KV cache on one node, so use FP8 there. Use the DSA tilelang backend (`--dsa-prefill-backend tilelang --dsa-decode-backend tilelang`) and add `--chunked-prefill-size 131072` plus `--watchdog-timeout 1200` (20 min for weight loading). GLM-5.3 and DeepSeek-V3.2 share the same model structure; for other DSA / HiSparse tips see the [DeepSeek-V3.2 cookbook](../DeepSeek/DeepSeek-V3_2).
 - **MTP / EAGLE speculative decoding** is disabled for AMD in the Deploy panel because the gfx950 spec-decode draft kernel is not yet validated on this hardware (and at `--speculative-num-steps > 3` hits a separate build issue). Until MTP is validated on gfx950, omit the `--speculative-*` flags and serve without MTP.
